$comment: ADR-0026 §3 outbound-fetch vectors. ONE fixture, TWO repositories, byte-identical. Edit the ToolYard copy, re-copy into LoadCoach, and prove it with cmp — the sha256 is asserted in both, so a drift is a failing test rather than a discovery. Nothing here is specific to either implementation: no credential vectors (ToolYard has no credential surface at all), no bare-origin or `since` vectors (LoadCoach's evidence endpoint, not a general fetch), and every size is written relative to the configured cap because the cap is 8 MiB in ToolYard and 128 MiB in LoadCoach.

fields.name: unique identifier; also the pytest parameter id
fields.why: the ADR-0026 §3 rule this vector pins
fields.allowed_hosts: the policy's host allowlist, always stated explicitly — the two implementations differ on what an EMPTY allowlist means (ToolYard: loopback only, spec §11.5; LoadCoach: nothing), so no vector leaves it out
fields.max_bytes: null means the implementation's configured default; an integer overrides it for this vector so a cap can be exercised without moving 128 MiB
fields.max_redirects: null means the implementation's default (3 in both)
fields.resolves: host -> addresses the injected resolver answers with. A host absent from this map resolves to nothing.
fields.responses: scripted, consumed in order, one per request the client makes. Each has status, headers, and one of body (literal text) or body_bytes_over_cap (a body of exactly cap + N bytes). `streamed: true` sends the body as chunks with NO Content-Length, which is the only way to reach the during-streaming check — a fixed body makes httpx declare a length, and the declared-length check would fire first and pass the test for the wrong reason. `declared_length_over_cap` sets Content-Length to cap + N explicitly.
fields.expect: {outcome: 'refused'|'failed'|'ok', reason: <the machine-readable reason both implementations must produce>, content_type: <for ok>}
fields.requests_expected: how many requests the client is allowed to have made — a check applied before a socket is opened must show as 0

vectors.name: a_file_url_is_refused_before_anything_is_resolved
vectors.why: §3: scheme in {http, https} only. file:// is a local read in a URL's clothing.

vectors.name: an_ftp_url_is_refused
vectors.why: §3: the scheme allowlist is closed, not a blocklist of file://.

vectors.name: a_url_naming_no_host_is_refused
vectors.why: §3: an allowlist needs a host to check. Refused before resolution.

vectors.name: a_host_outside_the_allowlist_is_refused_without_connecting
vectors.why: §3: a remote source must be listed explicitly — exposure is a deliberate act.

vectors.name: the_allowlist_is_matched_case_insensitively
vectors.why: §3: hostnames are case-insensitive, so an allowlist that is not would be bypassable by shouting.

vectors.name: a_literal_link_local_address_is_refused_even_when_allowlisted
vectors.why: §3: link-local is refused unconditionally — the cloud metadata range is the classic target. Being on the allowlist is not a second opinion.

vectors.name: an_allowlisted_name_that_resolves_link_local_is_refused
vectors.why: §3: 'and any address that resolves into them'. This is the vector a literal-only check misses.

vectors.name: a_name_resolving_to_several_addresses_is_refused_if_any_is_link_local
vectors.why: §3: one bad answer among good ones is still a bad answer. Order must not decide it.

vectors.name: an_ipv6_link_local_literal_is_refused
vectors.why: §3 names fe80::/10 alongside 169.254.0.0/16; a v4-only check is half a check.

vectors.name: a_redirect_to_another_host_is_refused
vectors.why: §3: redirects are not followed across a host change, and no credential is ever forwarded across one.

vectors.name: a_redirect_to_the_metadata_address_is_refused_even_when_it_is_allowlisted
vectors.why: The SSRF-through-redirect vector. Both implementations stop it at the host-change rule, which fires before the link-local rule — so an allowlist that names the metadata address does not open it.

vectors.name: a_redirect_that_changes_scheme_on_the_same_host_is_refused
vectors.why: §3: every hop is re-checked IN FULL, not merely for a host change. The host is unchanged here, so only a second scheme check catches it — this is the vector a first-hop-only check misses.

vectors.name: a_same_host_redirect_is_followed_once
vectors.why: §3 caps hops; it does not forbid them. The permitted case is pinned so a cap change cannot silently forbid all of them.

vectors.name: redirects_past_the_cap_are_refused
vectors.why: §3: total redirects capped. A same-host loop must terminate.

vectors.name: a_declared_content_length_over_the_cap_is_refused_before_the_body
vectors.why: §3: the size cap. The declaration is the origin's claim and it is checked first, so an oversized transfer is never begun.

vectors.name: a_body_that_outgrows_the_cap_is_stopped_mid_stream
vectors.why: §3: enforced DURING streaming, so an origin that declares no length at all — chunked, which is what a streaming export does — is still bounded. `streamed` is load-bearing: with a fixed body httpx declares a Content-Length and the earlier check fires instead, and this vector would pass without ever running the code it names.

vectors.name: a_chunked_body_within_the_cap_is_read_to_the_end
vectors.why: The streaming path's success case, so that tightening the mid-stream comparison cannot quietly refuse every chunked response.

vectors.name: a_body_exactly_at_the_cap_is_accepted
vectors.why: The cap is a limit, not an off-by-one. Pinned so tightening the comparison cannot go unnoticed.

vectors.name: a_content_type_outside_the_allowlist_is_refused_before_parsing
vectors.why: §3: Content-Type verified before parsing. The body here is deliberately malformed, so a check that ran after parsing would fail differently.

vectors.name: a_missing_content_type_is_refused
vectors.why: Default closed: an absent header is not a permissive one.

vectors.name: a_charset_parameter_does_not_defeat_the_content_type_check
vectors.why: The media type is the part before the semicolon; comparing the whole header would refuse every correctly-labelled response.

vectors.name: a_structured_json_suffix_is_admitted
vectors.why: RFC 6839's +json suffix is JSON. Both implementations admit it, so it is shared rather than left to drift.

vectors.name: a_server_error_is_a_failure_and_not_a_refusal
vectors.why: The REFUSED/FAILED line: the origin answered badly, no rule of ours declined anything, and retrying may be meaningful.

vectors.name: a_transport_failure_is_a_failure_and_not_a_refusal
vectors.why: Same line, the other side of it: the origin was never heard from.
